validity.recommendation: Existence, dates, status, classification, and location all corroborate; keep as-is.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: Confirmed real. A directly-fetched, verified primary source -- Sputnik Uzbekistan, 2021-11-29, carrying an official Ministry of Energy statement -- states verbatim: 'V dannyy moment v napravlenii Gazli-Kagan deystvuyut tri nitki gazoprovoda. Pervuyu i vtoruyu iz nikh zapustili eshche v 1973-1983 godakh, a tret'ya otkrylas' v 2006-m' ("Currently in the Gazli-Kagan direction three lines/strings of gas pipeline operate. The first and second of them were launched back in 1973-1983, and the third opened in 2006"). This matches GEM's segment_name 'Segment I, II' and StartYear1=1973/StartYear2=1983 exactly, and confirms the trunk ('magistral'nyy gazoprovod' = transmission) classification and Gazli->Kagan routing. A second independent source (Uzreport.news, 2021-05-21) separately names 'Gazli-Kagan' among Uzbekistan's active trunk gas pipelines undergoing a repair/modernization program (61 km of it scheduled for capital repair), corroborating active operating status from a different publisher. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: NOT a duplicate. The corridor carries (per the Sputnik ministry statement) three existing lines as of Nov 2021 plus a fourth then under construction. P2290 = lines I & II (this row, 1973/1983, combined). P3984 (len=116.0, dia=1020, cap=35.00) is the best fit for line III (opened 2006) -- an independent web search separately turned up an unrelated technical note describing a km0-10 + km78-116 (48 km) reconstruction at 1020 mm diameter completed 2005-2006, consistent with a line opening in that window, though I could not verify that note's URL directly and did not use it as a citation. P3983 (len=140.0, cap=25.00) matches the fourth line the Sputnik article describes under construction (140 km, ~100 km already built, expected to add 25 million m3/day) almost exactly. So the three same-named rows are genuinely parallel physical pipe in one corridor, not a mislabeling/double-count of P2290 -- consistent with the standing guidance that a parallel string is real pipe until a source affirmatively says otherwise. ATTRIBUTION: FuelSource=Gazli and StartLocation=Gazli/EndLocation=Kagan (both Uzbekistan) are self-evident from every source found (the pipeline is literally named for these two points) and independently corroborated by Sputnik + Uzreport. Operator=Uztransgaz could NOT be independently confirmed to the required standard -- see fills (UNRESOLVED).

validity.recommendation: Do not treat Capacity=35.00 as confirmed for this segment alone; check whether GEM's source attributed the whole-corridor throughput figure to this row (and possibly also to P3984) rather than a per-line split.
validity.researcher_notes: The only independent capacity figure I could find and verify (Sputnik, 2021-11-29, quoting the Ministry of Energy) is: 'po dannym ministerstva, za sutki cherez dannyy magistral'nyy gazoprovod prokhodit 35 mln kubometrov prirodnogo gaza' ("per the ministry, 35 million cubic meters of natural gas pass daily through this trunk gas pipeline") -- stated in the context of describing the corridor's THREE existing lines together (I/II from 1973-1983 plus III from 2006), i.e. it reads as the aggregate throughput of the whole Gazli-Kagan system as of late 2021, not a figure isolated to lines I & II. GEM's Capacity=35.00 on P2290 matches this number exactly, but so does P3984 (also Gazli-Kagan, presumptively line III), which is suspicious: if 35 is the system-wide aggregate, it cannot correctly belong to both a 'lines I,II' row and a 'line III' row simultaneously without double-counting corridor capacity. I found no source that breaks the 35 mcm/day figure down per individual line (I vs II vs III), in Russian or English, after a genuine search. Flagging rather than confirming; recommend Update leg check whether the two rows' capacities were sourced from the same 2021 statement.

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources describe Gazli-Kagan as an active trunk system: Sputnik/Ministry of Energy (Nov 2021) states 35 million m3/day is currently flowing through it; Uzreport (May 2021) lists it among trunk pipelines undergoing active capital-repair works (61 km) as part of an ongoing modernization program. Status inferred from operational context, not a literal word match, per standard practice.
Source refers throughout to 'gazoprovod' (gas pipeline) transporting 'prirodnyy gaz' (natural gas) -- straightforward confirmation.
Both sources call it a 'magistral'nyy gazoprovod' (trunk/main gas pipeline), i.e. transmission, not a gathering/distribution line.

Only one source found with these exact dates: 'Pervuyu i vtoruyu iz nikh zapustili eshche v 1973-1983 godakh' (the first and second [lines] were launched back in 1973-1983) -- but it is an official Ministry of Energy statement carried by a wire service, so treated as a single strong source (medium tier) rather than a weak one. A second candidate corroborating quote (tafsilar.info, archived copy citing the same 1973-1983/2006 figures) could not be independently re-verified: the live tafsilar.info page returns a client-side redirect stub, and its Wayback capture (20230129130734, confirmed to exist via the availability API) could not be fetched today -- web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this session on 2026-08-26, a known network condition (see country note), not evidence the capture is bad.

See validity concern (spec): the one figure I found (35 million Sm3/day, Sputnik/Min. of Energy 2021) reads as the whole-corridor aggregate (3 lines), not a lines-I&II-only figure, and the same number is also recorded on P3984. Not staging a ref for a value I cannot confirm is correctly scoped to this segment.

No independent source gives a length for lines I/II specifically (115.3 km). Sources found give lengths for other segments of the corridor (140 km for the new 4th line; a 48 km reconstruction span at km 0-10/78-116) but nothing for I/II. Genuine UNRESOLVED after a Russian-language search, not an English-only miss.

No independent source confirms 720/1020 mm for lines I/II specifically. A search turned up a 1020 mm figure tied to a 2005-2006 reconstruction of km 78-116 (48 km) -- plausibly line III territory, not lines I/II -- so I did not use it here to avoid misattributing another line's spec to this row.

The pipeline's own name and every source's routing description confirm it originates at Gazli (giant gas field / underground storage). No second source independently names Gazli as the specific fuel source beyond the shared pipeline name, so kept at medium tier.
Both Gazli and Kagan, Uzbekistan, are named directly as the pipeline's endpoints in both independent sources (the pipeline is named for its two termini).

Circumstantial support only: Uztransgaz's Gazli linear-production department page (gazligs.com) names Uztransgaz as operator of Gazli-area trunk infrastructure but does NOT name 'Gazli-Kagan' specifically (fails verifier's Gazli-Kagan token check), and utg.uz/ru/about/history/ is a confirmed dead link (404) per the country note. No page found both names Gazli-Kagan and states Uztransgaz operates it, so leaving unresolved rather than citing an adjacent-but-not-on-point page.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest independently-dated evidence found naming this pipeline is Nov 2021 (Sputnik, Ministry of Energy statement: 35 million m3/day currently flowing through the existing 3-line corridor) plus May 2021 (Uzreport: active in a capital-repair program). No indication of dormancy -- the corridor was in fact under active government investment (a 4th parallel line under construction 2021-2022) at the time of the newest evidence, which is the opposite of a stale signal. Well under any staleness threshold; sheet LastUpdated (2024-08-29) is itself newer than my found evidence, so no change proposed.

summary: P2290 (Gazli-Kagan lines I & II, 1973-1983): existence/classification/dates/status/location confirmed high-to-medium tier via 2 independent Russian sources (Sputnik/Min. of Energy 2021-11-29 + Uzreport 2021-05-21); NOT a duplicate of P3983/P3984 (parallel lines III/IV in the same corridor, each independently attested). One spec concern staged: Capacity=35.00 likely reflects the whole 3-line corridor's aggregate throughput rather than lines I&II alone, and is suspiciously duplicated onto P3984. UNRESOLVED after genuine RU search: Length, Diameter, Operator.
